subject: On-prem bare-metal networking: Terraform/Helm/Ansible module coordination and CI gating
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: noc@edgeops.io
Date: 2027-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: Bare-metal networking + IaC handoff (Redwood private deployment)

Irene / Redwood team,

Thanks again for agreeing to run the private deployment workshop next week. Before we lock the agenda, a quick practical ask: our on-prem site uses Broadcom NICs with SR-IOV on a subset of hosts and a mix of VLANs for tenant segmentation. We want to avoid last-minute network rework during the cutover.

Could you share a short proposal for how your Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules will: 
- Express SR-IOV and NIC-level config (preferably with defaults for Acme)
- Map tenants to VLAN ranges in a repeatable way in TF variables
- Integrate with our edge partner's provisioning (edgeops.io) for BGP peering and VRF configs

If useful, I attached a diagram of our current rack wiring and VLAN map. Our NOC (copied) will be on the call.

Target timeline: dry-run config validation on staging hosts by 2027-03-18, production cutover 2027-04-05 (flexible).

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Cloud Platform, Acme Financials

Attachment: acme-baremetal-networking-diagrams.pdf (diagram PDF, 1 file)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, noc@edgeops.io
Date: 2027-03-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Bare-metal networking + IaC handoff (Redwood private deployment)

Thanks, Samira — good context. Looping Marcus (infra runtime) and Mina (security & gating). Below are the high-level choices we'll propose for the workshop; we'll follow up with a short PR and CI gating checklist.

1) Representation of NIC/SR-IOV in Terraform
- We'll add an optional provider-level module (providers/baremetal/networking) that declares NIC profiles and a per-host "device_profile" var. Default will not touch SR-IOV unless a host is explicitly opted-in.
- The module will expose a map: { host_id => [device_profile] } so teams can pin profiles in environment tfvars.

2) VLAN/tenant mapping
- We'll provide a small helper module (networking/tenants) that takes a tenant id and returns VLAN ranges and subnet CIDRs. The mapping will be driven by a CSV-backed data source for easy bulk edits in non-prod and locked down in prod via a terraform state lock policy.

3) Helm + Ansible interactions
- Helm charts will be parameterized to read the networking annotations injected by an init Ansible playbook. The playbook will run post-provision to ensure switch port configs and host-level sysctl/networkd settings are consistent.

4) CI gating and validation
- We'll propose an integration pipeline step (GitHub Actions) that runs: terraform fmt/validate/plan (with a planfile), a dry-run Helm template + kubeval pass, and an Ansible --check run against a small ephemeral lab (via edgeops test harness). Failures block merge.

Marcus / Mina — quick asks: can you confirm the gating tests above are sufficient, and flag any additional security validation (Mina) or runtime perf tests (Marcus) we should include in the plan?

I'll open a proposal PR with the initial modules and sample tfvars before EOD so we can iterate.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-corp.com>, noc@edgeops.io
Date: 2027-03-07T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Bare-metal networking + IaC handoff (Redwood private deployment)

Short notes from infra runtime perspective — thanks for the outline. A few specifics I'd add: 

- SR-IOV fallback: the TF module should tag hosts with an "sriov_capable" boolean and create two variants of the network device resource: one that programs VF allocation (when true) and one that leaves NIC untouched. This avoids state churn when hosts are reprovisioned.

- BGP / edgeops integration: prefer to push only the abstracted BGP session object from TF to the edgeops API (via a small provisioner) rather than raw switch configs. Edgeops will own the actual switch template. This keeps our Ansible playbooks host-focused and avoids secrets duplication.

- Performance validation: include a post-provision micro-benchmark job (containerized, runs iperf3 + small latency tests) that runs in CI labs. Results should be uploaded to an artifact storage (we'll use the GH Action artifact + a short JSON summary). Fail gating only for regression >15% compared to baseline.

Attachment: tf-helm-ansible-proposal.diff (local diff patch with initial module skeleton)

I'll open a PR with the device_profile proto and a sample plan that targets a two-host lab.

– Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-corp.com>, noc@edgeops.io
Date: 2027-03-07T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Bare-metal networking + IaC handoff (Redwood private deployment)

Thanks — agree with Marcus and Irene. A couple of security/Gating additions from my side: 

1) Secrets handling: any edgeops API keys or switch management creds used by provisioners must be injected via the pipeline secrets store (not TF vars). Use short-lived tokens and rotate post-cutover.

2) Policy checks: add a pre-merge policy step (OPA/Conftest) that rejects any TF changes that: modify existing prod VLAN ranges, remove state locks, or change provider-level permission scopes.

3) Audit logs & evidence: we should capture the GH Action run logs and the Ansible --check outputs and push a summarized audit record (JSON) into the Acme compliance folder. That record will contain the plan SHA, who ran it, and artifacts.

Action items (quick):
- Marcus: open the PR for device_profile + perf job (you said you'd do this) — target: 2027-03-09
- Irene: create PR with gating workflow and initial OPA rules — target: 2027-03-08
- Samira / edgeops: confirm whether you prefer provider-level BGP sessions pushed via TF provisioner or via your API (Samira, quick reply ok) — target: 2027-03-09

I'll add the policy examples to the compliance doc once Marcus's PR lands.

Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
